_about: THE GROUND RULE's numbers (Track TK, 2026-10-10, finished by TK2 2026-10-11; scripts/sim/ground_rules.gd reads this and holds the rule, scripts/sim/world.gd applies it). A unit of domain 'ground' that can move (data/units: tank; the static batteries, the tower and the bridge never plan) stays on dry land. The World is GIVEN what it needs, as it is given the water (World.set_water): World.set_ground(level, road, woods, road_path) - Callables (x, y) -> the height level (0 low ground, 1 upland, 2 top), -> the metres to the nearest road centre line (INF when none is near), -> the tree density (0 to 1, the chance a dart becomes a tree), and (from, to) -> the road between two points (for the AI); scripts/world/ground_map.gd answers all four from the game's terrain and world layout. A rule part whose query is missing is off, and without any the sim is testable on its own. WHAT IT KEEPS, along every step a ground unit plans (the step's arc is sampled and at each sample the hull's centre and both ends are looked at): (1) EVERY HEIGHT STEP IS A CLIFF (ALEX, decision terrain-passability A: 'every height step is a cliff: impassable to ground units, crossed only at ramps or roads'; ramps do not exist yet): the hull stays on one height level, and the level under its centre changes between two samples only where the unit is on a road at both (on a road the hull may also straddle two levels); (2) NO WATER: the sea, the river and a pond are never driven into (the World's water query, set_water; wade_m deep is the most a ground unit fords), except over an INTACT BRIDGE (a unit of a bridge type that is not down): where the water is covered by the span, the deck is road; a destroyed bridge is water again; (3) THE GOING: the step's end speed may not exceed the unit's envelope speed_max_mps times a factor, averaged over the step: 1 on a road (so the top speed IS the road speed), speed_factor.open elsewhere, speed_factor.woods among trees (proposed: slower, never a block - Alex: trees do not block sight, and nothing says they block a tank). A step that breaks (1) or (2) is CLAMPED the way the envelope and the sea rule clamp: first SLOWED (the same turn at slower and slower end speeds, down to the floor of the step's speed window; slow_tries of them, then refined by bisection so the step is the fastest legal one), then, if even the slowest breaks it, HELD (the unit stays where it is, speed 0); the step reports clamped with the limit 'cliff' or 'water' (Envelope.LIMIT_CLIFF, LIMIT_WATER). A step the going slows reports 'terrain' (Envelope.LIMIT_TERRAIN): the cap is soft - a unit cannot brake faster than its decel, so one that drives from a road into woods at top speed is as slow as its brakes allow and no slower. THE PLANNER sees the same rule: World.reachable returns the fan clipped by it (for sea units too: the sea rule, data/sim/sea.json). A unit that STARTS in a pose that breaks the rule (placed in the river, on a cliff line) is held: a scenario places a tank on dry ground. EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track TK; none is a decision except the cliff rule (Alex).

hull_fraction._reason: the hull's ends are checked at this share of the unit's size_m ahead of and astern of its centre, along its heading (as the sea rule does for a boat): 0.5 is the front and the back of the tracks. A 6 m tank is therefore kept 3 m back from a cliff line and a shore, and its sprite does not overhang it

sample_m._reason: a step's arc is sampled at least this often (and at least four times, however short): a tank's step is 5 to 25 m, so a cliff line or a creek 4 m wide is not stepped over; the hull's 6 m length means two samples always see it too

slow_tries._reason: a step that breaks the rule is tried at this many slower end speeds, evenly spaced from the planned one down to the floor of the step's speed window, before the unit is held (the sea rule's four, finer because a tank's step is short and its stopping distance is a few metres)

refine_steps._reason: once a slower speed is legal, the step is refined by this many bisections between it and the last speed that was not, so a step into woods or onto a shore is the fastest legal one (to 1/16 of the ladder's gap, about 0.1 m/s for the tank) and the fan's edge is the real limit, not the nearest rung of the ladder

road_half_m._reason: a unit is ON THE ROAD when its centre is within this of the road's centre line: the drawn road's half width (data/params/render_defaults.json constants.road_half_width_px 16 at 2 px per metre) and a bridge's half deck (data/world/bridges.json deck_width_m 16)

wade_m._reason: the depth of water a ground unit may drive into: 0, none - any water under the hull (centre or either end) is a block. A ford would be a separate decision (and a bridge-free way across a river that the bridge mission's 'a destroyed bridge stops it' depends on not existing)

bridge_types._reason: the unit types that carry a ground unit across water while they stand (data/units/bridge.json). A unit of one of these that is down (destroyed) carries nothing. The span is the rectangle size_m long along the bridge's heading and bridge_half_width_m either side of its axis

bridge_half_width_m._reason: half the deck (data/world/bridges.json deck_width_m 16, the road's own width): a hull centre and both ends within it, across the bridge's axis, are on the span

speed_factor._about: Top speed (the unit's envelope speed_max_mps) as a share of itself, by the going under the hull's centre. A road is 1: the unit's top speed IS its road speed.

road._reason: the lead's brief for the tank: about 10 m/s on a road, so the road is the unit's own top speed; the bridge's deck counts as road

open._reason: bare ground, fields and the village streets off the road: half the road speed (5 m/s for the tank, 12.5 m in a step): a tank can cross country, it is just slow, and the road is a reason to use the road. Fields and rough ground are not told apart yet

woods._reason: among trees (the density below): a smaller share again, 3 m/s for the tank, and never a block (trees do not block sight 'for now', Alex, and nothing says they block a tank). The drawn trees are not obstacles to it either, as the planes' shadows are not

woods_density_min._reason: the tree density (terrain.gd's rule: the chance a dart becomes a tree, (f - threshold) x gain on the level) at or above which the ground counts as woods: an even chance of a tree per dart. Below it the ground is open, so a stray tree does not slow a tank but a grove does
